text.first-impression: Sin, people meet you and think: put together. The outfit, the posture, the very specific coffee order. You notice everything and you're polite about it, mostly. Ten seconds in, people can tell you have taste, and maybe also that you're slightly judging their shoes. You are. We both know you are. What they don't see: you're sensitive. Very. A careless comment can sting for days behind a perfectly composed face, and you'll replay it while doing your skincare, word by word. Maybe tell someone when it happens, out loud, on the day.
text.your-red-flag: Your red flag: perfectionism with a side of silent judgment. You have standards for everything, and you grade everyone quietly, then feel disappointed when they fail criteria they didn't know existed. You also take small slights personally and keep them polished in a little display case, lit nicely, labelled by date. People think you're cool and above it. Actually, you're hurt and far too elegant to say so. That's a lot of energy spent on looking unbothered when you could just mention it. Saying that stung is extremely chic, actually.
text.how-you-sabotage-love: In love you want to be treasured, and you should be. But you sometimes test people instead of telling them what you need. Your sabotage is falling for an ideal and then being let down by the real, slightly chaotic human. You also play it cool when you care, waiting hours to reply so you seem unbothered. Unbothered isn't attractive. Honest is. Real people have flaws. So do real jewels, by the way. They're called inclusions, and they're how you tell a real stone from a fake one. Be the real one.
text.friends-and-work: At work you deliver quality: polished, precise, impeccable. Also slow, because nothing is ever finished, it's just abandoned at 2am when you finally give up on perfect. Criticism hurts far more than you let anyone see. With friends you're thoughtful, the perfect gift giver, the one with the excellent recommendations. But you can be picky about friends to the point of loneliness. Not everyone needs to be fully polished to be worth keeping. Some of the best people are a bit rough around the edges. Let a few of them in.
text.the-lie: The lie you tell yourself: I just have high standards. Sometimes it's high standards. Sometimes it's fear of being seen trying and failing in public. You also tell yourself you're fine alone because people are disappointing. Some are, sure. But some would genuinely surprise you if you let them see the unpolished version: the bad day, the messy room, the unfiltered opinion. That version is more lovable than you think. It's certainly more interesting. Show one person the messy draft of you this month. Watch them like you more, not less. It's almost annoying how well it works.
text.the-fix: The fix, approved by Bom. Finish something at ninety percent and send it anyway. Tell one person something that hurt, right when it happens, in plain words. Do one thing badly on purpose: karaoke, a sketch, dancing at a wedding. In love, say what you need instead of testing whether they'll guess. You're a jewel: rare, sharp, beautiful. You don't need to be flawless to be precious. Nobody does. Not even you. Especially not you. Okay, that was almost sweet. Moving on. Seriously, ninety percent is plenty. Nobody else can see the last ten.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Sin. You've judged three outfits and a font since we started.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Great taste. And a secret scorecard nobody agreed to.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: You play it cool when you care. Unbothered isn't a love language.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: True. Now do karaoke badly. On purpose. Character building.

spring.intro: Spring Sin, Wood ran your birth season and Metal shapes Wood, so you're a jewel in a shop full of options with opinions about every single one. Stylish, sharp and very particular. People clock your taste in ten seconds. Your red flag is the eternal upgrade. Nothing is ever quite right: the restaurant, the outfit, the partner. You're always browsing. In love you keep one eye on the exit in case something better comes along. At work you redesign the project before finishing it. The fix: pick something, commit and stop comparing for a month. Contentment is a skill, and you've been skipping practice.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You returned the same jacket three times. Then you bought it again. Sin.

summer.intro: Summer Sin, Fire ran your season and Fire tests Metal, so you were polished under heat and now you flinch at every spark. You're elegant, gracious and secretly devastated by mild feedback. People see someone composed and stylish. Your friends know one comment about your haircut ruined your week. Your red flag is sensitivity disguised as poise. You smile, then replay the comment for days and quietly withdraw. In love you take small criticism as total rejection. At work you go icy when someone edits your work. The fix: when feedback stings, ask whether it's about you or about the thing. It's usually the thing.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Someone said 'interesting fringe' and you thought about it for nine days, Sin.

autumn.intro: Autumn Sin, Metal ran your birth month and doubled your element, so you're the jewel in the glass case and you'd like everyone to admire from a distance. Refined, proud, exquisite taste. People find you a bit intimidating. Your friends know you're softer than you look and would never admit it. Your red flag is pride as a security system. You don't apologise easily, you don't ask twice and you never chase. In love partners feel judged. At work your standards are brilliant and also exhausting for everyone near them. The fix: say I was wrong once this month, sincerely, with no clever follow-up line.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You'd rather eat glass than say sorry first. Try it once, Sin. Glass optional.

winter.intro: Winter Sin, Water ran your season and Metal generates Water, so your sparkle comes out as wit. Dry, precise, slightly devastating. People see someone clever and a bit aloof. Your friends know your one-liners are how you avoid saying anything real. Your red flag is sarcasm as armour. Someone gets close, you make a joke. Someone compliments you, you deflect with a better joke. In love partners get your best material and none of your actual feelings. At work you're the funniest person in the room and the hardest to read. The fix: next time you feel something, say it straight before you reach for the punchline.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Sin is so funny! Sin is also allowed to say something sincere.

strength.strong: Strong chart, Sin. Well set, well polished and very aware of it. The blind spot: you're a snob, darling. Lovingly. Your standards are high enough that people feel judged walking into your flat. In love you notice the shoes, the grammar, the restaurant choice, and you mark points off silently. With friends you're the self-appointed arbiter of taste. The fix: compliment something you'd never choose yourself, sincerely. Taste isn't one correct answer, and joy isn't a design award. Let people enjoy their beige sofas.
strength.weak: Weak chart, Sin, so your sparkle depends a lot on outside lighting. Translation: you need reassurance more than you admit. The blind spot: perfectionism as protection. If everything you post, say and wear is flawless, nobody can criticise. Exhausting. In love one careless remark lands like a crack in the stone. At work you over-prepare and still feel like a fraud. The fix: post something unedited. Send a message without rereading it four times. Discover that people like you scratched.

balance_text.too_much_wood: Too much Wood. You're all growth, plans and ambition, and you never stop reaching. Cute. Also exhausting. You start projects faster than you finish them, and you think rest is for people with fewer goals. You argue to win rather than to understand. Yeon's prescription: prune. Finish one thing before starting another. Say you're right once a week and mean it. A tree that never stops growing eventually just falls over.
balance_text.missing_wood: Missing Wood. Starting things is hard for you, so you just... don't. You wait for the right moment, and the right moment is apparently very busy. You have plans in drafts and ideas in your notes app from three years ago. Yeon's prescription: take the first ugly step today. Send the email. Sign up for the class. Buy the plant. Momentum isn't a mood. It's a decision you make before you feel ready.
balance_text.too_much_fire: Too much Fire. Everything's urgent, everything's dramatic, and your feelings arrive with sirens on. You're fun and bright, and you're also impulsive, and you've sent messages you'd love to unsend. Yeon's prescription: wait one night before any big decision. Drink water, literally and spiritually. Let your calmest friend talk you down before your wildest one hypes you up. Your spark is great. Your house fires are not.
balance_text.missing_fire: Missing Fire. You're lovely, but you're keeping your light on its dimmest setting. You hang back, never celebrate yourself, and assume people won't notice you anyway. That isn't modesty. It's hiding with good manners. Yeon's prescription: be seen. Post the thing, wear the colour, tell the joke out loud. Go outside in the sun. People can't love what they can't see, and you're worth seeing.
balance_text.too_much_earth: Too much Earth. You're stable. Very stable. Possibly too stable. Same restaurant, same route, same opinion, same worry on repeat. You call it reliable. It's also a rut with nice furniture. Yeon's prescription: one new thing a week. It doesn't have to be big. A new food, a new walk, a new person to talk to. Growth needs a little mess, and you can tidy it up afterwards if it makes you feel better.
balance_text.missing_earth: Missing Earth. You're a little all over the place. Plans change, meals get skipped, home is wherever you last dropped your bag. You're adaptable, sure, but you never quite feel settled. Yeon's prescription: routine. Boring, beautiful routine. Same bedtime, real meals, one corner of your home that's only yours. Grounded people make better decisions. Yes, I'm looking directly at you.
balance_text.too_much_metal: Too much Metal. You're sharp, critical, and your opinions come with edges. You decide fast and judge faster. People respect you, and also slightly fear your face in meetings. Yeon's prescription: soften up. Ask before you judge. Let some things stay imperfect. Cry at a film. You can keep your standards and still let people near you without running a full security check first.
balance_text.missing_metal: Missing Metal. Boundaries? Never heard of them. You say yes when you mean no, answer messages at midnight, and lend people your time without ever getting it back. Yeon's prescription: one no a week, with no explanation attached. Declutter something. Unsubscribe, unfollow, unclench. A boundary isn't mean. It's just a door with a lock, and you're allowed to own the key.
balance_text.too_much_water: Too much Water. You think. And think. And then think about what you thought. You feel everything and analyse it until it turns to soup. Your intuition is brilliant. Your sleep schedule is not. Yeon's prescription: get out of your head and into your body. Walk, cook, lift something heavy. Put a timer on the overthinking. Then go and live a little.
balance_text.missing_water: Missing Water. You go, go, go and never stop to feel anything. Rest is for the weak, reflection is a waste of time, and you've been busy for about five years straight. Yeon's prescription: sit still. Ten minutes. No phone. Write one honest line before bed. Your feelings don't disappear because you're running. They just wait for you, patiently, like a bill.

too_much_wood.speaker: yeon
too_much_wood.text: Too much Wood. You started a new life plan on Monday. It's Wednesday. New plan.

too_much_wood.speaker: bom
too_much_wood.text: All that drive is wonderful. Finishing one thing will feel even better.

too_much_fire.speaker: yeon
too_much_fire.text: Too much Fire: three dramatic exits from group chats this year. I counted.

too_much_fire.speaker: bom
too_much_fire.text: Your passion lights rooms up. Count to ten before the big reply.

too_much_earth.speaker: yeon
too_much_earth.text: Heavy Earth: same order, same route, same hoodie since 2019. I see you.

too_much_earth.speaker: bom
too_much_earth.text: Your steadiness makes people feel safe. Try one new thing for fun.

too_much_metal.speaker: yeon
too_much_metal.text: Lots of Metal. Your honesty has made two baristas reconsider their careers.

too_much_metal.speaker: bom
too_much_metal.text: Your clarity is a gift. Wrap it in a little kindness.

too_much_water.speaker: yeon
too_much_water.text: Overflowing Water: you've overthought this reading three times already. Stop.

too_much_water.speaker: bom
too_much_water.text: Your depth is beautiful. Come back to shore when it gets heavy.

missing_wood.speaker: yeon
missing_wood.text: No Wood, no ambition. Your five-year plan is 'see what happens'.

missing_wood.speaker: bom
missing_wood.text: Missing Wood just means growth needs a nudge. One small goal is plenty.

missing_fire.speaker: yeon
missing_fire.text: No Fire. You'd describe your best night out ever as 'fine'. Show some spark!

missing_fire.speaker: bom
missing_fire.text: Missing Fire can mute your joy. Do one thing just because it's fun.

missing_earth.speaker: yeon
missing_earth.text: No Earth. You've changed flat, job and hair colour twice this year.

missing_earth.speaker: bom
missing_earth.text: Missing Earth makes it hard to settle. A simple routine is grounding.

missing_metal.speaker: yeon
missing_metal.text: No Metal. You've never said no to anyone in your life, have you?

missing_metal.speaker: bom
missing_metal.text: Missing Metal means boundaries take practice. Start with one tiny no.

missing_water.speaker: yeon
missing_water.text: No Water. Someone cried in front of you and you offered a snack.

missing_water.speaker: bom
missing_water.text: Missing Water can hide feelings. Name one out loud today.
